Subject: Sharp p95 increase for model omega-v2 — urgent

Jonas,

We started seeing a sharp rise in p95 latency for requests routed to model: omega-v2 after the 02:00 UTC rollout. Over the last 90 minutes p95 has moved from ~220ms to ~1.1s for our prod workloads (text-generation). This is beyond our SLA (p95 < 500ms) and is causing timeouts in downstream validation.

Can you confirm whether this was expected for the v2 weights/quant changes? If not, we need either an immediate rollback to omega-v1 or activation of the stability gate to fallback to omega-v1 while you investigate.

Attached: p95-delta-omega-v2-20270521.csv (sampled traces)

Amir Patel
FinMetric Ops

Thanks for the heads up, Amir — and for the CSV. We’re treating this as an escalated latency regression. I’ve looped in SRE (Markus) and Product (Karthik) to validate whether the observed delta is expected from the recent quantization tweak.

Short answer: we can enable the stability gate and route FinMetric traffic back to omega-v1 immediately, but we need SRE sign-off on the traffic-shift plan and confirmation of rollback triggers.

Proposed immediate actions:
- SRE to run a quick diagnostic on the deploy and verify no hot-path kernel fallback is causing the spike (Markus)
- If diagnostic is inconclusive or confirms regression, authorize staged traffic reweight: 100% -> 50% v2 / 50% v1 -> 10% steps to v1 over 30 mins (canary-style)
- Apply automatic rollback triggers: p95 > 700ms for 2 consecutive 5-min windows OR error-rate delta > 1.5x baseline

Please confirm you want us to proceed with the stability gate activation now; if yes, we’ll begin the staged traffic shift and send ETA for each step.

-Jonas

Jonas / team,

Quick SRE assessment after looking at the traces and runtime metrics: the increase aligns with the quant path taken by omega-v2 for sequence lengths > 512. We see an increased number of kernel fusions falling back to non-optimized kernels under the current GPU kernel selector for that shape. That explains the ~5x p95 delta in the attached sample.

We can execute the stability gate fallback now. Proposed operational playbook (attached: canary-playbook-omega-v2.pdf):
- Pre-checks (5m): validate no stuck RPCs, cluster health ok, warm caches on omega-v1 nodes
- Step 1 (T+0): route 20% of FinMetric traffic to omega-v1, 80% to v2; monitor 5-minute windows
- Step 2 (T+10m): if p95 < 600ms, move to 50/50; otherwise abort and shift to 100% v1
- Step 3 (T+20m): if stable, complete to 100% v1 and keep v2 pinned in canary for debug

Rollback / abort triggers (automated):
- p95 > 700ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows
- 5xx rate increase > 1.5x baseline
- CPU/GPU load > 95% for > 2m on v1 cluster during shift (safety net)

ETA to complete full fallback (if needed): ~25-40 minutes depending on monitoring windows. Will collect diagnostic bundle for Product after shift.

(attachment: canary-playbook-omega-v2.pdf)

-Markus
